declared.title: Ironic processes in the mental control of mood and mood-related thought.
declared.foundIn: reports/chasing-happiness/counter-evidence.md (card 1); Europe PMC search TITLE:"ironic processes in the mental control of mood" (2026-11-22)

population: participants of two lab experiments (1993); sample sizes and country not given in the abstract

findings.text: People asked to make their mood better (or worse) while recalling an event managed to, when their mind was free

support.sentence: Ss attempting mood control without an imposed cognitive load were successful, whereas those who attempted control while rehearsing a 9-digit number not only failed to control their moods but also showed self-reported mood change opposite the mood they intended to create.

findings.text: Under mental load (holding a 9-digit number), trying to change one's mood failed and the mood moved the opposite way

support.sentence: Ss attempting mood control without an imposed cognitive load were successful, whereas those who attempted control while rehearsing a 9-digit number not only failed to control their moods but also showed self-reported mood change opposite the mood they intended to create.

limits: the abstract pools attempts to make one's mood positive and negative
small lab samples of 1993; no replication on mood found (2026-11-22)
a few minutes of mood control while recalling one event, not wanting happiness in one's life
